name: Unubahe
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2012. Change Request 2012-142: create [unu] Unubahe (submitted by Brian Paris, SIL-PNG; supporters M. Rueck, J. Brownie). 5 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; states that all information comes from Rueck's report.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2012. Request for New Language Code Element in ISO 639-3: unu, Unubahe (alternate name Unoba'i). 4 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; says the language is unattested in the literature apart from one mention as 'Unoba'i' in a 1997 survey report and that no written literature or recordings exist; closest languages Buhutu [bxh] and Oya'oya [oyy].

sources.citation: Rueck, Michael J. 2001 (posted as undated draft). Unubahe: A nearly extinct language? 11 pp. SIL-PNG survey wordlist report; SIL Language & Culture Archives item 49168 (www.sil.org/resources/archives/49168).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The report is a speaker census plus two wordlists (a 70-item list in the speaker's own spelling, and the SIL-PNG 190-item list in IPA, elicited 14 Aug 2001). IPA transcriptions carry vowel length and glottal stop but no stress marks; the only phonological remarks are footnotes on possessive suffixes and on non-contrastive l ~ flap.

sources.citation: Rueck, Michael J. 2001. Original field recordings / survey notes for the Unubahe 190-item SIL-PNG wordlist (Dagama village, 14 Aug 2001), if archived at SIL-PNG Ukarumpa.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: If audio of the elicited wordlist survives in the SIL-PNG survey archive, stress could be determined instrumentally; no written description exists.

sources.citation: Cooper, Mary, Beth Evans, Marie Keliah & Clif Olson. 1997. SIL Milne Bay Sociolinguistic Survey of the Naura Language. Manuscript. SIL: Ukarumpa.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only other document known to mention the language ('Unoba'i'); unpublished SIL-PNG survey manuscript. Low expectation of any stress statement (Rueck says it mentions the name only), but it is the sole remaining lead.
